Local Website Editor data-edit-path

Hover over teksten om te zien welke onderdelen straks aanklikbaar worden in de editor. Deze uitleg is System-tekst en daarom bewust niet bewerkbaar.

Concept

A website as content canvas

Visitors see a normal website. The editor opens the Local Website Editor on its own URL, clicks text, edits it, and writes the changes back to the same JSON files that 11ty uses to build the site.

Editor

Editable building blocks

1

Text per element

Every heading, paragraph and button label has its own path in JSON, so the editor does not need to understand HTML.

2

Multilingual per field

NL, EN and DE live under the same content element. The page can be viewed and edited per language.

3

11ty stays in control

Templates, partials and build output remain plain 11ty. The editor becomes a layer on top, only for local content changes.

Lokaal

Suggested workflow

1

Open the local site

The editor opens the 11ty preview and turns edit mode on.

2

Click text

The editor reads `data-edit-path` to know which JSON field belongs to the clicked element.

3

Save locally

A small Node API writes the change back to JSON. Then 11ty rebuilds the site.

JSON

Content model

All manageable content on this page comes from `src/_data/content.json`. The attributes on the HTML elements point back to the exact same place in that file.

src/_data/content.json -> pages.home.hero.title.en

SEO

SEO belongs in the foundation

Non-visible fields such as SEO title, meta description, canonical, Open Graph and hreflang also belong in the content model. They are not always clickable in the editor, but they are rendered from JSON.

title + description + canonical + Open Graph + hreflang
